# Scope: Unified Linux Package & App Manager

Scope is a desktop app for Linux that unifies APT, Snap, Flatpak, and AppImage into one list to see, update, and uninstall every app, regardless of how it was installed. It is built with Rust and Zed's GPUI, no webview.

## Pages

- [Homepage](https://khurrambhutto.github.io/scope/): Overview, features, download links, and FAQ for the Linux app manager.
- [GitHub Repository](https://github.com/khurrambhutto/scope): Source code, issues, and releases.
- [Releases](https://github.com/khurrambhutto/scope/releases): Pre-built `.deb` bundles.

## Key Information

- **License**: MIT
- **Platform**: Linux (Ubuntu / Debian first)
- **Stack**: Rust, Zed's GPUI
- **Author**: Khurram Bhutto (https://khurrambhutto.tech/)
- **Features**: Unified package list across APT, Snap, Flatpak, and AppImage; desktop-entry and icon enrichment; preview-first uninstall and update with Polkit privilege escalation

## Installation

Download the `.deb` from [Releases](https://github.com/khurrambhutto/scope/releases). The app checks the Releases API on startup and self-updates (`.deb` via `pkexec dpkg -i`); installs it can't self-update fall back to the Releases page. To build from source, install `libxkbcommon-x11-dev` and run `cargo run`.

```bash
curl -LO https://github.com/khurrambhutto/scope/releases/latest/download/scope_0.3.1_amd64.deb
sudo apt install ./scope_0.3.1_amd64.deb
```

## FAQ

**What is Scope?**
A desktop app that unifies APT, Snap, Flatpak, and AppImage into a single list for seeing, updating, and uninstalling installed software.

**Which package managers are supported?**
APT (Debian/Ubuntu), Snap, Flatpak, and AppImage.

**Is it free?**
Yes, MIT licensed open source software.
